package.title: Memory stocks trade the calendar, not the news
package.promised: An explanation of why memory-stock prices seem to rise and fall on a predictable calendar rather than reacting directly to headlines. I expect to learn which points in the memory cycle matter and why the market anticipates them.

new_things: Memory-stock prices are said to trade around a calendar rather than directly on news.
Around the fifteenth of each month, Korean customs publishes memory-chip export prices.
That monthly print is presented as an important timing signal for memory-stock investors.
Hynix and Micron are said to move around the print before it comes out, not afterward.
reports.held_question: Why does that Korean customs price print matter enough for the market to anticipate it?

new_things: The comparison covers 25 monthly prints from August 2024 through August 2026.
In the half-month before the print, the stocks averaged a 6.8% gain.
The video is comparing gains before versus after the monthly print.
reports.held_question: What is the average gain in the half-month after the print, and does that show the move mostly happens beforehand?
reports.asked_of_me: Watch where the month's gain actually lands.
could_not_follow: The after-print average is cut off after 'plus two point'.

new_things: The two weeks after the print averaged a 2.2% gain.
The move is described as front-run, so a strong print is already reflected in prices.
After 14 strong prints, the following two weeks averaged a 3.4% gain.
Eight of those 14 strong-print periods were up.
There were eight weak prints in the 25-month period.
reports.held_question: What happened to the stocks after the weak memory-price prints?

new_things: After seven of the eight weak prints, the stocks fell.
After weak prints, the average stock move was down 6.9 percent.
The latest weak print was in July, and stocks fell 14 percent over the following two weeks.
The chip price was 16 percent higher one month after that latest weak print.
The video calls this mismatch between stock performance and chip-price performance asymmetry.
reports.held_question: Why do weak prints punish the stocks even when the chip price itself rises afterward?

new_things: Good news is already priced in before the print arrives.
Bad news is the remaining surprise that can move stocks.
The key is knowing the earnings-print calendar rather than reading the print faster than the market.
Stocks trade the print on the day it lands.
reports.held_question: When is the next print due?
reports.asked_of_me: Know the calendar for when the print lands.
